uncited: Unlike [Axis-Aligned Bounding Box Geometry](1317-axis-aligned-bounding-box-geometry.md) which renders wireframes or solid boxes, this method rasterizes specific faces to simulate a 3D view without full ray-marching.
- A 2D image where each pixel column corresponds to a diagonal slice of the voxel volume.
- The voxel model is accessed as `model[x, y, z]`.
The rendering is performed in two passes or variants: the basic Diagonal pass and the Diagonal Peek pass.
Both iterate over screen coordinates `(pixelX, pixelY)`.
-   The basic logic above is extended with a `peek` boolean parameter in the drawing functions.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(W \cdot H \cdot D)$ where $W, H, D$ are the dimensions of the voxel grid, as each diagonal line is scanned.
The inner loop runs until a voxel is found or boundaries are hit.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary memory, excluding the output image buffer.
The peek feature helps visualize the top surface of volumes.
The diagonal projection can distort perception of depth compared to perspective views.
- **When to use:** Debugging voxel data, quick visualization of large voxel grids, educational purposes.
- **When not to use:** Production-quality rendering, scenes requiring accurate lighting or shadows.
It is designed for debugging and visualizing voxel data in a 3D-like manner.
